rates-unicode-16-digit-date.reason: Adopt for #197, pinning the check command of rates.py, whose package script moves to bench-tools rates check, through a driver that points the retained library at the case directory and its --source pages, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-18. Old behavior: rates.py validated as_of with rates.schema.json's ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ and parsed it with datetime.strptime and %Y-%m-%d, whose year and day patterns use \d, so the digits it accepted depended on the interpreter's Unicode database. New behavior: bench-tools rates check is fixed at the Unicode 16.0 decimal digits (category Nd) that Python 3.14 reads. Rationale: a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: an as_of changes when written with a digit the former interpreter's database lacks. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is the 80 digits added in Unicode 16.0 (U+10D40..U+10D49, U+116D0..U+116E3, U+11BF0..U+11BF9, U+16130..U+16139, U+16D70..U+16D79, U+1CCF0..U+1CCF9, U+1E5F1..U+1E5FA). Older interpreters lack more: Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) lacks 110, those 80 and 30 added in Unicode 14.0 and 15.0 (U+11F50..U+11F59, U+16AC0..U+16AC9, U+1E4F0..U+1E4F9). No tracked file, rates.json and rates.current.json included, contains any of the 110. This case pins acceptance: on Python 3.13 or older (Unicode 15.1 or earlier), rates.py refused this catalog, exit 1, because as_of did not match the schema pattern; Rust checks it, as Python 3.14 does. Resolving issue: #197.

Old behavior: a value made of a dash, digits and dots, such as -.5, was read as a value, as argparse reads a negative number. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads a dash-led argument as a value only when it parses as a number with a digit before any dot, so -.5 is an unexpected argument, exit 2; -5 and -1.5 remain values. Rationale: allow_negative_numbers has no setting for argparse's rule, and emulating argparse would keep the hand-written parsing #215 removes; no caller passes such a value. Compatibility impact: give the value attached, as --rates=-.5, which still works; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/rates.py, the retained library, read -.5 as the catalog, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. Resolving issue: #215.

rates-exponent-rates.reason: Adopt for #30, by the repository owner's direction, delegated through orchestration on 2026-10-24: the provider changed its standard pricing table and every Codex dispatch was refused. Supersedes decision-f8016c4c511c9c7152f50f00384bb8044116de6bbf751385e3f7d3154c0b0a13 and changes the OpenAI page only. Old behavior: the page's standard table had the columns Model, short-context input, cached input, cache writes and output, then the same four for long context, and gpt-6.1-sol's cache-write price filled both catalog write fields. New behavior: the page has the provider's 2026-10 columns, Model, short-context input, output, cached input, 30m write and 12h write, then the same five for long context; the 30-minute write, the provider's default cache lifetime, fills both catalog write fields, and the opt-in 12-hour write is not read. The prices read, the catalog, the expected output and the exit code are unchanged. Rationale: bench-tools rates reads the live page, which no longer serves the old table, so the old layout now refuses as a changed table. Compatibility impact: a saved copy of the old page now exits 1 with 'provider pricing columns changed'; frozen runs execute their own pinned code and are unaffected. Resolving issue: #30. The baseline_defect keeps the old page, as the deleted Python observed it.

rates-help-after-extra-argument.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Rationale: clap's parser reports an unexpected argument when it reads it; deferring it would need hand-written parsing #215 removes. Compatibility impact: a command line with an extra argument fails even when it also asks for help; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/rates.py, the retained library, printed help, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. rates-help-with-attached-argument.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name rates.py. Changes behavior on purpose, toward Python. Old behavior: bench-tools rates refused -hx, an argument attached to -h, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap reads -hx as -h then -x and prints help, exit 0, as argparse does under Python 3.12 and 3.14 when the attached text, after any further h's, starts with neither = nor -; build-packet already printed help. -h or a run of h's with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h-x or -hh=1, is still refused, exit 2, as argparse refuses it, which rates-help-with-equals-or-dash records. Rationale: clap's short-option rule. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now prints help and runs nothing; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/rates.py, the retained library, printed help too, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. This supersedes rates-decisions.v9.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

rates-help-with-equals-or-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name rates.py. Keeps the exit code and changes the message. Old behavior: bench-tools rates refused -h with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h=, -h- and -h-x, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap would print help for them, exit 0, so main.rs refuses an -h before -- whose attached text, after any further h's, starts with = or - when clap is about to print help, with clap's error: prefix, argparse's message argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1', and the subcommand's usage, exit 2. Rationale: argparse under Python 3.12 and 3.14 refuses these spellings with that message, exit 2, and prints help only for spellings such as -hx, -hhx and -hxh=1, whose attached text after the h's starts with neither. Compatibility impact: none for exit codes; only the diagnostic wording changes; under Python 3.12 and 3.14, bench/tools/rates.py, the retained library, refuses them with argparse's usage-first wording, which this case's baseline_defect records; the differential reports the difference as an approved fix. This supersedes rates-decisions.v9.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

rates-help-before-invalid-short-help.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools rates: --help before -h=1 prints the help and exits 0, because argparse acts on --help as soon as it reads it. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench/tools/rates.py printed argparse's help and exited 0, where bench-tools refused the later -h=1 with exit 2. New behavior: bench-tools rates prints clap's help and exits 0; main.rs refuses -h, or a run of h's, with an attached = or - argument only when it is the first help before --, for every subcommand. Rationale: argparse acts on the first help it reads, so an earlier --help, or a unique prefix of it such as --hel, wins over a later -h=1. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches Python's; only the help wording differs, as for every bench-tools help. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #268.

rates-invalid-command-before-help.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools rates: An invalid command before --help is refused with exit 2, because argparse checks the command's choices as it reads it, before the later --help. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: bench/tools/rates.py refused the command with exit 2, where bench-tools printed its help and exited 0, as it checked the command only after parsing. New behavior: bench-tools rates checks the command while parsing and refuses it with exit 2 and the message it prints for the invalid command alone. Rationale: argparse's choices=('check', 'refresh') refuses another command as it reads it. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches Python's; the message keeps bench-tools' wording, which names only check because refresh is refused separately, and clap's usage. Python 3.12 lists the choices unquoted and 3.14 quotes them, so the observation pins the stderr prefix both print; the exit code agrees. Resolving issue: #268.
